outcome: Preeclampsia and eclampsia superimposed on hypertension
Venous thromboembolism (deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism during pregnancy, intrapartum, or postpartum)
cohort: 14,881 women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and 298 women with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) from the Health Care Cost and Utilization Project-Nationwide Inpatient Sample database (HCUP-NIS) from 2004 to 2014
finding: Women with PCOS were at increased risk of developing pregnancy-induced hypertension and gestational diabetes compared to women with CAH, while women with CAH were at increased risk for delivery via cesarean section and small for gestational age neonates.
mod_finding: Women with CAH were at increased risk for delivery via cesarean section.
